known_limits: Coarse by construction: with one eval video per category, a 2/1 partition necessarily leaves categories unrepresented. Here dev covers case_study + live_session and holdout covers concept only, so dev-vs-holdout differences confound 'sealed vs not' with 'concept vs the rest'. Design doc section 5.3 accepts this explicitly ('with 16 videos, any split is coarse'); the fix is more mined videos, not a cleverer partition of three.
A single holdout video means the holdout estimate has wide error bars. Use it as a release-candidate sanity check, never as a precise number, and never for run-over-run iteration.
No within-video splitting is used or permitted (design doc section 5.3): adjacent keyframes share narration, context, and phrasing, so a record-level split would score generalization we do not have.
procedure: This file subdivides split-v1.json's eval_videos into dev + holdout. It does NOT restate or alter v1's train/eval boundary: train_videos are read from the parent at build time, and tooling refuses any v2 whose dev+holdout is not exactly the parent's eval_videos.
1. Take the parent's eval_videos and sort them lexicographically, so the input order of a JSON list can never influence the outcome.

2. Shuffle with random.Random(f'{seed}:v2') where seed = 20260725 (the date this file was created; distinct from v1's 20260724 so the partition is not correlated with the shuffle that produced v1's train/eval boundary).
3. The first round(n/3) entries (minimum 1, capped at n-1) are the holdout; the remainder are dev. With n=3 this is 2 dev / 1 holdout.

Not stratified by category: with exactly one eval video per category, stratification degenerates -- see known_limits. Reproduce with stoic_training.splits.partition_eval_videos(parent['eval_videos']).
quarantine_rule: Newly mined videos -- present in the corpus but named by neither this file nor its parent -- are quarantined into the HOLDOUT pool by default (design doc section 5.2: they are the truly-unseen future). Split files are immutable, so the enforcement point is the dataset builder: stoic_training.build_dataset detects unknown videos, refuses to build unless --allow-corpus-drift acknowledges the corpus has moved, and then routes them into eval_holdout.jsonl while printing the quarantine report. --on-new-videos fail turns that into a hard error. A new video is never silently routed into train or dev, and never silently dropped.
seal_rule: eval_holdout.jsonl is SEALED: stoic_training.evaluate refuses to score it without --unseal "<reason>", which appends run id, ISO date, eval set and reason to splits/unseal-ledger.md. Budget: single-digit unsealings per split version.
